summary: Chi-chiang Huang specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. Huang completed a PhD at the University of Arizona in 1986 under the supervision of Jing-shen Tao and studied with Robert M. Gimello.

Chi-wah Chan works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Chan earned a PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles in 1993, having studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman, and served as a Teaching Assistant at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Chie Ikeya is a historian and archaeologist who earned a PhD from Cornell University in 2006, where she studied under David K. Wyatt.

Chien Y. Hsu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies under Leslie S. Kawamura (through 2011) and James B. Apple, and studied under the traditional teacher Zhenhua (attested 2013).

Chien-hsing Ho specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Ho served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University (attested 2014) and held a post at Academia Sinica (attested 2018).

Chih-fu Li works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Li served as Director of the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2007) and later became its honorary director, having retired on December 26, 2006.

Chih-mien Adrian Tseng is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at McMaster University under James A. Benn, also advised by Nobuyoshi Yamabe and Canshan Cheng. Tseng has held faculty posts at Fo Guang University.

Chijo Akamatsu (1886–1960) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo. Akamatsu served as a professor at Ryukoku, Koyasan, Hanazono, Keijo Imperial (1927–1941), and Yamaguchi universities, and lectured at Kyoto and Kyushu.

Chikafumi Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's at the University of British Columbia and a PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, also studying under Karin Preisendanz, Ashok Narhar Aklujkar, and others.
Chiko Corona is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Kenko Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura.

Chikyo Yamamoto (1910–1993) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Yamamoto held positions at Koyasan University, serving as a professor in 1970 and as a part-time lecturer in 1980.
Chime Rinpoche (1941–2026) was an expert in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Gangshar, taught Pema Chödrön, and held a post at the British Library.

Chin Kung (1927–2022) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who founded the Hwa Dzan Buddhist Library and Corporate Body of the Buddha Educational Foundation. He served at Chinese Culture University and headed the Pure Land Learning College Association.

Ching Keng is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology who earned a PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil. Keng later served as Associate Professor at National Chengchi University (~2013–2019).

Ching-mao Cheng (1933–2025) was a scholar of Sinology and Japanology who earned a PhD from Princeton. Cheng held posts at UC Berkeley, chaired Asian Languages and Literatures at UMass Amherst, and was a founder and founding chair at National Dong Hwa University.

Ching-mei Shyu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. Shyu completed an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi under Jan Nattier and a PhD at Cornell University in 2008 under Daniel Boucher, Hubert Durt, and Jane-Marie Law.
Chirapat Prapandvidya (born 1941) works in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. Prapandvidya founded Silpakorn University, served as its Director in 1996, and taught Kazuhiro Yamamoto.

Chisan Kohō (1879–1967) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyodo Koshuin. He held leadership posts at Saijō-ji Senmon Sōdō, Nagano Ken Senmon Nisodo, and Soji-ji, and founded Tsurumi Women's University in 1966.
Chishō Namai (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Namai served as a professor (attested 1996) and later as president (attested 2008) of Koyasan University.

Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1964–1968). Takenaka served as an associate professor at Hanazono University (~1975–1989) and as a professor at Tokoha University (~1989).
